subject: general
concept: Awards and Honours, Science Technology and Inventions
question: Hideki Yukawa, who received the Nobel Prize in 1949, is well known for which discovery?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Theory of nuclear forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hideki Yukawa **is renowned for his **groundbreaking theory of nuclear forces,** particularly his prediction of the **existence of mesons**.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1949** for this significant contribution to the field.
 
• In 1935,** Yukawa **published his theory of mesons, elucidating the interactions between protons and neutrons.
 
• His theory was inspired by the discovery of a specific type of meson in cosmic rays by American physicists in **1937**.
 
• Yukawa's work established him as one of the most influential theoretical physicists of the 20th century and earned him the distinction of being Japan's first Nobel laureate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meghnad Saha,** an Indian astrophysicist, is renowned for his development of the theory of thermal ionization in 1920. Thermal ionization is a physical phenomenon wherein atoms are desorbed from a heated surface and subsequently ionized.
 
• **Homi Jehangir Bhabha**, an Indian nuclear scientist, is celebrated for his research on the cascade process of cosmic radiation. This process involves a sequence of secondary interactions occurring when cosmic rays collide with air nuclei in the upper atmosphere.
 
• **Alessandro Volta** is credited as the first individual to create an electric charge storage device using metal disks and acid-dipped cardboard. This invention laid the foundation for the development of the standard unit of electric charge in the International System of Units (SI), known as the coulomb (C).
